record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^2, and consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem Delta u + lambda u = 0 in Omega with u = 0 on ∂Omega. If u_2 is any second eigenfunction, must its nodal line {x in Omega : u_2(x) = 0} fail to be a closed curve?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 (Payne). Let n = 2, for any second eigenfunction u2 the nodal line {x ∈ Ω | u2(x) = 0} is not a closed curve.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² be a bounded connected open set, and consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem
   Δu + λu = 0 in Ω,    u = 0 on ∂Ω.
Let λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ... denote the Dirichlet eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity), and let a "second eigenfunction" mean any non-trivial solution u₂ associated with the second eigenvalue λ₂. The nodal set of u₂ is N(u₂) = {x ∈ Ω : u₂(x) = 0}.

Prove or disprove: for every such Ω and every second eigenfunction u₂, the nodal set N(u₂) is not a closed curve contained in Ω (equivalently, the nodal set must reach the boundary ∂Ω).
artifact.status_search_result: For general bounded connected planar domains, the conjecture is false: Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Hoffmann-Ostenhof and Nadirashvili (1997) constructed a multiply connected counterexample, and subsequent work (Dahne–Hoffmann-Ostenhof–Hoffmann-Ostenhof–Salvy, 2021; recent 2025 work) reduced the number of holes, with a counterexample on a doubly-connected domain announced in arXiv:2510.24436. The conjecture remains open for simply connected planar domains; it has been proved for convex domains (Melas; Alessandrini).

status_evidence.title: A counterexample to Payne's nodal line conjecture with few holes
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample with a small number of holes; the original conjecture was disproved by Hoffmann-Ostenhof–Hoffmann-Ostenhof–Nadirashvili in 1997.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is false for multiply connected planar domains.

status_evidence.title: Payne's nodal line conjecture fails on doubly-connected planar domains
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a doubly connected planar domain whose second Dirichlet eigenfunction has a closed nodal line.
status_evidence.claim: A counterexample exists with only one hole, so the conjecture can hold at most for simply connected domains.

status_evidence.title: On the nodal line conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing positive results for convex and simply connected domains and the open status in the simply connected case.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture proved for convex domains; remains open for general simply connected domains.
